correctness.rationale: Use regular decagon circumscribed about radius-one disk, normals n_j=(cos(jπ/5),sin(jπ/5)), and facet x=(1,t), |t|≤tan(π/10). For each facet-interior Birkhoff pair, the support functional forces y=±(0,sec(π/10)). A vertex-first pair swaps to facet-first owing to the regular 4m+2 Radon incidence and symmetry of F(x,y). On this entire facet segment the upper supports for x+y and x−y are n_1 and n_9, respectively, so F=(cos(π/5)+sin(π/5)sec(π/10))sin(π/5)t; the slope is positive. I separately evaluated all ten support linear forms at t=−tanα,0,tanα and verified the asserted active supports (linearity makes endpoints sufficient for whole segment). The endpoint norms are (1+√5)/2 and √5−1, so F=(5√5−9)/8. This is an exact continuum reduction; finite endpoint checks verify linear support dominance, not a substitute for global reasoning.
residual_risks: The proof uses special vertex/facet symmetry for regular decagon, not arbitrary 10-gon.
The endpoint norm assertions depend on the support region; full region verified by convex linear inequalities.
